function: p. 4, 13: Grid-less multi-source DOA estimation from unknown uplink data symbols with sparse arrays; the DOAs prune downlink beam-sweeping candidates (sensing-assisted MU-MIMO beam management).
system: p. 9-10: BS with 5-element (aperture 10) or 15-element (aperture 79) minimum-redundancy sparse linear array, far-field narrowband sources; 64-element ULA for beam management (p. 14); no RIS; 15 GHz.
method: p. 7-10: Attention-only transformer on raw snapshots (Snap-TF, 2-3 layers, d_attn=96, permutation invariant), supervised end-to-end training with SGD, 100 epochs, on simulated data.
data_channel: p. 4, 9-10: Custom simulated far-field array-response model with random path losses, uniform DOAs, Gaussian or 16QAM symbols; 2e6 training samples per K; no 3GPP or measured channel.
test_conditions: p. 10-11: Trained with SNR in [-20,20] dB, T=50, 16QAM; tested at SNR -30 to 20 dB, T=10-100, and mixed QPSK+16QAM, without retraining.
baselines: p. 10, 12, 14: Learned DOA methods DCR-T, DCR-G-Fro, DCR-G-Aff, SRL-GD (CNN covariance reconstruction plus Root-MUSIC); DCR-E2E ablation; Oracle Root-MUSIC on a 10-element ULA; full codebook sweeping.
metrics: p. 4, 14: DOA MSE (rad^2) versus SNR; runtime and trainable parameters; downlink system throughput versus coherence time; beam-sweeping overhead.
complexity: p. 9, 12: Order O(ceil(log2(k+1)) T^2 d_attn); runtime 1.103 ms (M=5) and 1.112 ms (M=15); about 0.356 million parameters versus 11-17 million for benchmarks.
openness: none; the paper releases no code or data and only uses the open-source toolbox of baseline [34] (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "narrowband and far-field sources" impinging on a linear array; custom array-response model with random path losses (p. 9). No 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "Despite being trained at T = 50, Snap-TF achieves superior performance for 20 ≤ T ≤ 100"; also tested on mixed QPSK+16QAM not seen in training, without retraining. The SNR sweep is not counted.
q3_support: p. 10: "For the benchmark algorithms (DCR-T [33], DCR-G-Fro [32], DCR-G-Aff [32]" and SRL-GD, earlier learned DOA methods compared on MSE (Fig. 5). Non-learned: p. 12 fn. 7 "applying Root-MUSIC to the sample SCM of a physical 10-element ULA" (Oracle, MSE) and p. 14 "Codebook only (full sweeping)" (throughput).
q4_support: p. 12: "is around 0.356 million in both setups" for the 3-layer Snap-TF, and "approximately 1.103 ms" runtime (Fig. 8); order O(ceil(log2(k+1)) T^2 d_attn) stated on p. 9.
q5_support: p. 15: "sharing the codes of [34]" concerns the baseline code only; no link or DOI for the authors' own code, and the training data are simulated (p. 10), with no public dataset.
notes: Borderline function check, flagged for the reviewer. The learned model is a DOA estimator (localization), which is excluded when it stands alone. It is proposed as include, area 5, because the paper frames it as ISAC (sensing reuses uplink data symbols, p. 1, 4) and evaluates sensing-assisted MU-MIMO beam management by downlink throughput (pp. 13-14). The pruning rule |theta_m - theta_k| < delta is not learned (p. 14), so exclude (function) is the alternative reading. q3 is met through the Oracle Root-MUSIC reference (p. 12) and full sweeping (p. 14) for the non-learned side; every curve of Fig. 5 is a learned method, and no plain MUSIC on the sparse array is plotted.
